**Luka Modrić** (Croatian pronunciation: [[lûːka mǒːdritɕ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-5) born 9 September 1985) is a Croatian professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [central midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder#Central_midfielder "Midfielder") for [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") club [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") and [captains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_\(association_football\) "Captain \(association football\)") the [Croatia national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_football_team "Croatia national football team"). He is widely regarded as one of the greatest midfielders of all time and as the greatest [Croatian footballer in history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Croatia_international_footballers "List of Croatia international footballers").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-xx1-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-xx2-7) With 34 major trophies, he is the [most decorated Croatian player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_association_football_records "List of world association football records") in world football. His career longevity ranks him joint-second globally for [all-time international appearances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men's_footballers_with_100_or_more_international_caps "List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps") and among the players with the highest number of [official matches ever played](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men's_footballers_with_1,000_or_more_official_appearances "List of men's footballers with 1,000 or more official appearances"), making him the first and only Croatian to reach the 1,150-appearance milestone.
Modrić began his career with Croatian club [Dinamo Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNK_Dinamo_Zagreb "GNK Dinamo Zagreb") from 2003 to 2008 – intermittently on loan to [Zrinjski Mostar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C5%A0K_Zrinjski_Mostar "HŠK Zrinjski Mostar") and [Inter Zaprešić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NK_Inter_Zapre%C5%A1i%C4%87 "NK Inter Zaprešić") – winning six domestic trophies. He moved to [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") in 2008, leading them to [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") qualification in 2010, the club's first qualification in almost 50 years. Modrić joined [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") for a £30 million transfer fee in 2012. He won the [2013–14 Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League") title and was named in the [squad of the season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League#Squad_of_the_season "2013–14 UEFA Champions League"). Modrić was a key member of the team's three consecutive Champions League titles from [2015–16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Champions_League "2015–16 UEFA Champions League") to [2017–18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League "2017–18 UEFA Champions League"), named to the squad of the season each time. In total, he won 28 major trophies with the club, including six UEFA Champions League titles, four [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") titles, and two [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") titles, making him [Real Madrid's all-time most decorated footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Real_Madrid_CF_records_and_statistics#Titles "List of Real Madrid CF records and statistics").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-8) He joined AC Milan in 2025 on a free transfer.
Since his international debut in 2006, Modrić has led the nation's "[second Golden Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_football_team#Dali%C4%87_period_\(since_2017\) "Croatia national football team")" of players. He has participated in every major tournament Croatia has qualified for, including every [UEFA European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") from [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008") to [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024 "UEFA Euro 2024"), as well as the [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup"), [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"), [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup"), [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") and [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup "2026 FIFA World Cup"). At Euro 2008, he was named in the [Team of the Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008#UEFA_Team_of_the_Tournament "UEFA Euro 2008"). Modrić led Croatia to a second and third-place finish at the 2018 and 2022 World Cup respectively, securing two [World Cup medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_awards "FIFA World Cup awards"). He individually won the [Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Golden_Ball "FIFA World Cup Golden Ball") as the tournament's best player in 2018, later winning the [Bronze Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Bronze_Ball "FIFA World Cup Bronze Ball") as the tournament's third-best player in 2022. Modrić similarly led the team to a silver medal in the [2023 UEFA Nations League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Nations_League_Finals "2023 UEFA Nations League Finals").
Throughout his career, Modrić has won numerous individual awards, culminating in the [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d'Or "Ballon d'Or") in 2018, making him the first player other than [Lionel Messi or Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messi%E2%80%93Ronaldo_rivalry "Messi–Ronaldo rivalry") to win the award since 2007. He has been named [Croatian Footballer of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_Footballer_of_the_Year "Croatian Footballer of the Year") a record fourteen times between 2007 and 2025. Modrić received the [Best FIFA Men's Player Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Best_FIFA_Men's_Player "The Best FIFA Men's Player"), the [UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Men's_Player_of_the_Year_Award "UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award"), and the [IFFHS World's Best Playmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFFHS_World's_Best_Playmaker#The_World's_Best_Playmaker "IFFHS World's Best Playmaker") award in 2018. He has been named in the [FIFPRO World 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFPRO_World_11 "FIFPRO World 11") six times and in the [UEFA Team of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Team_of_the_Year "UEFA Team of the Year") three times. In 2019, he was awarded the [Golden Foot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Foot "Golden Foot") for his personality and career legacy.
## Early life

Luka Modrić was born on 9 September 1985 in Zadar and was raised in the hamlet of Modrići, which is a part of [Zaton Obrovački](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaton_Obrova%C4%8Dki "Zaton Obrovački"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAzpitartePuertas201620-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTE%C4%8Cop201415-10) a village situated on the southern slopes of the mountain [Velebit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velebit "Velebit"), north of the city of [Zadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zadar "Zadar") in [SR Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Republic_of_Croatia "Socialist Republic of Croatia"), then a republic within [SFR Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Holiga2012-13) He is the oldest child of Stipe Modrić from Modrići and Radojka Dopuđ from [Kruševo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kru%C5%A1evo,_Zadar_County "Kruševo, Zadar County") near [Obrovac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obrovac,_Croatia "Obrovac, Croatia"), both of whom initially worked in a knitwear factory.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAzpitartePuertas201617,_20,_22-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Nacional-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-17) Modrić mostly spent his early years in the stone house where his paternal grandfather usually lived after whom he was named,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAzpitartePuertas201620-9)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTE%C4%8Cop201416-18) located on the road above the hamlet of Modrići,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTEModri%C4%87Matteoni20205%E2%80%936-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-21) and was shepherding goats as a five-year-old.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-ElvirUEFA-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-24)
His childhood coincided with the [Croatian War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_War_of_Independence "Croatian War of Independence")—in 1991, when the war escalated, his family were forced to flee the area.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11) Modrić's grandfather Luka was executed by [Serb rebels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Log_Revolution "Log Revolution") who were part of the police of [SAO Krajina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAO_Krajina "SAO Krajina") in December 1991 near his house in Modrići,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Holiga2012-13)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MakingofModric-26) and after the family fled, the house was burned to the ground.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAzpitartePuertas201621%E2%80%9322-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-28) Modrić became a refugee and lived with his family in the Hotel Kolovare for seven years; he later moved to the Hotel Iž, both in Zadar.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Boboska-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MarcaBio2017-30) His father joined the [Croatian Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_Army "Croatian Army") as an aeromechanic.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAzpitartePuertas201622-31) In those years, thousands of bombs [fell on the city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Zadar "Battle of Zadar") and football was a way to escape the reality of war.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Holiga2012-13) He recalls it as a tough time for his family and something which shaped him as a person.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Nathanson-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-AlanSmith-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BoyMarca-34) He said he was mostly unaware of the war because he befriended many other children and their parents did not let it affect their childhood.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Nacional-16)
In these difficult circumstances, Modrić began playing football, mostly at the hotel parking lot.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Holiga2012-13) In 1992, he simultaneously entered the primary school and a sporting academy, the latter paid for with the little money the family had, sometimes helped by Modrić's uncle.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Boboska-29)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Nacional-16) As a boy he was inspired to play football by [Zvonimir Boban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zvonimir_Boban "Zvonimir Boban") and [Francesco Totti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francesco_Totti "Francesco Totti").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-ready_to_play-35)
## Club career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Club career") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section's source code: Club career")]
### Early years
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early years") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section's source code: Early years")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Zadar_%2820069585463%29.jpg/250px-Zadar_%2820069585463%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zadar_\(20069585463\).jpg)Modrić began his youth career at [NK Zadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NK_Zadar "NK Zadar") in the city of [Zadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zadar "Zadar").
Supported by his family, Modrić participated in representative camps and trained at [NK Zadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NK_Zadar "NK Zadar").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Nacional-16) He was under the tutelage of coach Domagoj Bašić and the head of the youth academy, Tomislav Bašić.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11) Tomislav Bašić, considered by Modrić as his "sporting father",[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MakingofModric-26)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MarcaBio2017-30) said Modrić's father made him wooden shin guards because they had little money.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Nathanson-32)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BoyMarca-34) However, Modrić later denied the story.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Holiga2012-13) Due to being considered too young and light, he was not signed by Croatian powerhouse [Hajduk Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HNK_Hajduk_Split "HNK Hajduk Split"), the most representative football club in the region of [Dalmatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalmatia "Dalmatia").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Nacional-16)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-36) After displaying some talent, including at a youth tournament in Italy,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MakingofModric-26) Tomislav Bašić arranged Modrić's move to [Dinamo Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNK_Dinamo_Zagreb "GNK Dinamo Zagreb") when Modrić was a 16-year-old in late 2001.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Holiga2012-13)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37) After a season with Dinamo Zagreb's youth side, Modrić was loaned in 2003 to [Zrinjski Mostar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C5%A0K_Zrinjski_Mostar "HŠK Zrinjski Mostar") in the [Bosnian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stvaran-11)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MakingofModric-26) During this period, he established his versatile style of play and became the Bosnian Premier League Player of the Year at only the age of 18.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mid-38) Modrić later said, "Someone who can play in the Bosnian Premier League can play anywhere," referring to its physical nature.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mid-38) The following year, he was loaned to Croatian side [Inter Zaprešić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NK_Inter_Zapre%C5%A1i%C4%87 "NK Inter Zaprešić"). He spent one season there, helping the team to achieve second position in the [Prva HNL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Croatian_First_Football_League "2004–05 Croatian First Football League")[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MakingofModric-26)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-39) and a place in the preliminary round of the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_UEFA_Cup "2005–06 UEFA Cup"). He also won the [Croatian Football Hope of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_Footballer_of_the_Year#Croatian_Footballer_of_the_Year_\(1991%E2%80%93present\) "Croatian Footballer of the Year") award in 2004.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mid-38) He returned to Dinamo Zagreb in 2005.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mid-38)
### Dinamo Zagreb
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Dinamo Zagreb") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section's source code: Dinamo Zagreb")]
In the [2005–06 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_Croatian_First_Football_League "2005–06 Croatian First Football League"), Modrić signed a ten-year contract (his first long-term contract) with Dinamo Zagreb.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mid-38) With the contract's earnings, he bought a flat in Zadar for his family.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Holiga2012-13)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MakingofModric-26) He secured a place in Dinamo's first team, contributing 7 goals in 31 matches to help win the league.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-NFT-40) In the [2006–07 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_NK_Dinamo_Zagreb_season "2006–07 NK Dinamo Zagreb season"), Dinamo again won the league, with Modrić making a similar contribution.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-NFT-40) He was the main provider for striker [Eduardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_da_Silva "Eduardo da Silva"),[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mid-38) which helped Modrić win the [Prva HNL Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prva_HNL_Player_of_the_Year_\(Tportal\) "Prva HNL Player of the Year \(Tportal\)") award.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Real_Profile-3) The following season, Modrić as a team [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_\(association_football\) "Captain \(association football\)"),[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-41) led Dinamo's attempt to qualify for the [2007–08 UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Cup "2007–08 UEFA Cup"). In the final play-off stage, Modrić converted a penalty in the second and away fixture against [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax"); the match finished 1–1 after regular time. Dinamo won the match and play-off with a score of 3–2 after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_\(sports\) "Overtime \(sports\)") with two goals from teammate [Mario Mandžukić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Mand%C5%BEuki%C4%87 "Mario Mandžukić").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-42) However, Dinamo Zagreb failed to advance beyond the group stage. In his last home match with the club at [Maksimir Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maksimir_Stadium "Maksimir Stadium"), Modrić was given a standing ovation and fans held up supportive banners.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-44) He finished his four-year tenure at Dinamo with a tally of over 31 goals and 29 assists in four league seasons,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MakingofModric-26)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-45) contributing most notably in the [2007–08 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_NK_Dinamo_Zagreb_season "2007–08 NK Dinamo Zagreb season") when Dinamo won the second [Croatian Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Croatian_Football_Cup "2007–08 Croatian Football Cup") and became champions by a 28-point margin.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-46) Modrić was courted by [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"), [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") and [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C."), but opted to wait leaving the club.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MakingofModric-26)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Wilson2016-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Dutch-48)
### Tottenham Hotspur
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Tottenham Hotspur") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section's source code: Tottenham Hotspur")]
#### 2008–2010: Struggle and success in England
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2008–2010: Struggle and success in England") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section's source code: 2008–2010: Struggle and success in England")]
[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/05/Luka_Modri%C4%87_spurs.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Luka_Modri%C4%87_spurs.jpg)Modrić lining up for [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") in August 2008
Modrić agreed to transfer terms with [Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") on 26 April 2008. He was the first of many summer signings for manager [Juande Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juande_Ramos "Juande Ramos"), and was also the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Premier_League "2008–09 Premier League")'s first summer transfer.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-49) Club chairman [Daniel Levy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Levy_\(businessman\) "Daniel Levy \(businessman\)") promptly flew to [Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagreb "Zagreb") when [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") and [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.") became interested,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Stand-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-51) and after signing a six-year contract, Tottenham confirmed the transfer fee paid was £16.5 million, equalling the club's record fee set by [Darren Bent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Bent "Darren Bent")'s move in 2007.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-52) He got the [number 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_number_\(association_football\) "Squad number \(association football\)") [jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kit_\(association_football\) "Kit \(association football\)"), later recalling that he wore it in honour of [Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff "Johan Cruyff").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MarcaFFInterview-53) Modrić made his competitive Premier League debut on 16 August in a 2–1 defeat to [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.") at the [Riverside Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside_Stadium "Riverside Stadium") in Spurs' first match of the [2008–09 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2008–09 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-54)
Modrić had a slow start at Tottenham. He suffered from a knee injury early in his tenure and was labelled as a light-weight for the Premier League by sections of the media,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-AlanSmith-33) as well as Arsenal manager [Arsène Wenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ars%C3%A8ne_Wenger "Arsène Wenger").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Ice_Cold-55) Reflecting on that, Modrić said that such "critics push you forward to show people they are wrong. Maybe I look lightweight but I am a really strong person mentally and physically, and I never had any problems with my size".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37) This coincided with his poor form, leading to concerns both for himself and Croatia national team head coach [Slaven Bilić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slaven_Bili%C4%87 "Slaven Bilić").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Ice_Cold-55) Modrić spent his early days at the number 10 position, before being shifted to the left wing to play alongside [Wilson Palacios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Palacios "Wilson Palacios").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Ice_Cold-55) Spurs teammate [Tom Huddlestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Huddlestone "Tom Huddlestone") later said, "[H]is versatility was probably a blessing and a curse, he was that good that he had to play out of position for a bit."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Ice_Cold-55)
After the appointment of manager [Harry Redknapp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Redknapp "Harry Redknapp"), Modrić was given a more familiar role as a central or left-sided midfielder, allowing him to have more influence on the team and use his footballing talent more productively, for example in a 4–4 draw with [arch-rivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_London_derby "North London derby") Arsenal on 29 October.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-56) Redknapp recognised Modrić's value to his side and planned to shape his new team around the Croatian playmaker. He scored his first competitive goal at Tottenham in a 2–2 draw against [Spartak Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Spartak_Moscow "FC Spartak Moscow") during the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008-09_UEFA_Cup "2008-09 UEFA Cup") group stages on 18 December 2008.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-57) He scored his first Premier League goals against [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.") in an away defeat on 21 December, a home win in the [third round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_FA_Cup "2008–09 FA Cup") of the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup") against [Wigan Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") on 2 January 2009, and in an away defeat against [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") on 25 April 2009.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-58) Using Modrić in his former position from his Dinamo days made him more effective with performances against [Stoke City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_City_F.C. "Stoke City F.C."),[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-59) [Hull City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_City_A.F.C. "Hull City A.F.C."),[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-60) and most notably on 21 March when he scored the only goal in a win against Chelsea.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-61)
Before the [2009–10 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2009–10 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season"), Redknapp said of Modrić, "[He's] a hell of a player and a manager's dream, so I am told. He trains like a demon and never complains, will work with and without the ball on the field and can beat a defender with a trick or with a pass. He could get into any team in the top four".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-62) On 29 August 2009, during Tottenham's 2–1 win over [Birmingham City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_City_F.C. "Birmingham City F.C."), Modrić was taken off injured with a suspected calf injury.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-63) The following day, it was confirmed Modrić had sustained a fracture to his right [fibula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibula "Fibula") and was expected to be out for six weeks.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-64) He returned on 28 December in the [London derby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_derbies "London derbies") against [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."), which Spurs won 2–0 with an 11th-minute goal scored by Modrić using the leg he had broken.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-65) He again scored in a home win against [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C.") on 28 February 2010,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-66) and in an away defeat against [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") on 9 May.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-67) On 30 May 2010, Modrić signed a new six-year contract that ran until 2016. Upon signing, he said, "Tottenham Hotspur gave me my chance in the Premier League and I want to go on to achieve great success here with them. Yes, there have been enquiries from other big clubs, but I have no interest in going anywhere. Last season's top-four finish was an indication of where we are as a club and I feel I can continue to improve and go on to achieve everything I want to at Spurs."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-68)
#### 2010–2012: Final seasons in England
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2010–2012: Final seasons in England") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section's source code: 2010–2012: Final seasons in England")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Luka_Modri%C4%87_2010_2.jpg/250px-Luka_Modri%C4%87_2010_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Luka_Modri%C4%87_2010_2.jpg)Modrić playing against Arsenal in November 2010
On 11 September 2010, Modrić scored his first goal of the [2010–11 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2010–11 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season") in a 1–1 away draw at [West Bromwich Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bromwich_Albion_F.C. "West Bromwich Albion F.C.").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-69) On 28 November, in a home match against [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C."), Modrić scored a goal that was later credited as an [own goal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Own_goal "Own goal") by [Martin Škrtel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_%C5%A0krtel "Martin Škrtel"). After a draw against Manchester United at [White Hart Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Hart_Lane "White Hart Lane") in January 2011, Redknapp praised Modrić, saying, "He was unbelievable. Magnificent. He's an amazing footballer, the little man takes the ball in the tightest areas with people around him, wriggling out of situations. He could play in any team in the world."[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-70) Modrić also scored in Tottenham's 3–2 victory over Stoke City on 9 April,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-71) and converted a penalty at [Anfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anfield "Anfield") on 15 May in a 2–0 victory over Liverpool.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-72) Modrić helped Tottenham reach their first involvement in the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_UEFA_Champions_League "2010–11 UEFA Champions League"). In the first match, against [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") at the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro") on 20 October, he exited the match early due to injury; Spurs lost 4–3, despite the tremendous efforts of [Gareth Bale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Bale "Gareth Bale").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-73) On the return match at home, on 2 November, Modrić was given too much space to move and dictate the tempo of the match. He created and assisted for the first goal by [Rafael van der Vaart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_van_der_Vaart "Rafael van der Vaart") in a 3–1 victory.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-75) In the next match, against [Werder Bremen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SV_Werder_Bremen "SV Werder Bremen"), Modrić scored the second goal.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-76) After a scoreless draw against [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-77) Spurs were eliminated from the competition in the quarter-finals by [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-78)
Modrić played 32 Premier League matches in the [2010–11 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Premier_League "2010–11 Premier League"), scoring three goals, recording two assists and making the highest average number of passes per match for Spurs with 62.5 and an accuracy rate of 87.4%.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-79) At the end of the season, Modrić was voted the [Tottenham Hotspur Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C.#Player_of_the_Year "Tottenham Hotspur F.C."). Then-Manchester United manager [Sir Alex Ferguson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Ferguson "Alex Ferguson") said he would have chosen Modrić as his [Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFA_Players'_Player_of_the_Year "PFA Players' Player of the Year") for that season.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-80)
> "I spent four great years there with a lot of emotions, with a lot of love from the club and the fans. I enjoyed every moment with Tottenham. But in one moment you feel you need to take a step forward, to go to a higher level. I think it was the right time for me to go, but I will always be thankful to Tottenham for everything they did for me. I became a better player there and they pushed me to this level where I am at the moment."
— Luka Modrić reflecting on the negotiations with Chelsea and the move to Real Madrid in February 2014.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37)
In mid-2011, Modrić was heavily pursued by Tottenham's [London rivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C.%E2%80%93Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._rivalry "Chelsea F.C.–Tottenham Hotspur F.C. rivalry") Chelsea, who made a first bid of £22 million, which they increased to £27 million, both of which were rejected by Spurs chairman Daniel Levy.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-82) After the failed bids, Modrić announced he would welcome a move across London and that he had a "gentleman's agreement" with Levy the club would entertain offers from a "big club".[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-83) Speculation continued throughout the summer transfer window, culminating in Modrić refusing to play in Tottenham's opening match of the [2011–12 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2011–12 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season") against Manchester United, which ended in a 3–0 loss.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-84) Modrić said his "head was not in the right place" as he continued to force a move to Chelsea.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-85) On the final day of the transfer window, Chelsea made an offer of £40 million that was again rejected.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-86)
After failing to secure a transfer, Spurs manager Harry Redknapp told Modrić to focus on his playing and named him as a starter.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-87) On 18 September, he scored his first goal of the season for Tottenham with a shot from 23 m (25 yd) in a 4–0 home win against Liverpool.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-88) On 14 January 2012, Modrić scored the only goal in a home draw with [Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C. "Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-89) On 31 January in a 3–1 win against Wigan Athletic, he assisted for the first goal with a crossfield pass and scored the second from 18 m (20 yd).[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-90) For the third time that season, he was included in "Team of the Week".[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-91) Modrić scored his last goal for Tottenham on 2 May in a 1–4 away win against [Bolton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolton_Wanderers_F.C. "Bolton Wanderers F.C.") with a powerful volley from 23 m (25 yd).[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-92)
### Real Madrid
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Real Madrid") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section's source code: Real Madrid")]
#### 2012–13: Becoming a starter at Real Madrid
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2012–13: Becoming a starter at Real Madrid") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section's source code: 2012–13: Becoming a starter at Real Madrid")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Luka_Modri%C4%87_against_Sevilla.jpg/250px-Luka_Modri%C4%87_against_Sevilla.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Luka_Modri%C4%87_against_Sevilla.jpg)Modrić playing against [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") in February 2013
On 27 August 2012, Real Madrid announced they had agreed on a deal with Tottenham for an approximate £30 million transfer fee.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBCRM-93) Modrić signed a five-year contract with the Spanish club.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBCRM-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-94) Two days later, he made his Real Madrid debut against Barcelona in the second leg final of the [2012 Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2012 Supercopa de España") at the [Santiago Bernabéu Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium"), replacing [Mesut Özil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesut_%C3%96zil "Mesut Özil") in the 83rd minute. Madrid won the match, giving Modrić his first trophy with the club 36 hours after his signing was announced.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-95) Despite his positive debut, Modrić at first struggled to settle into the team under manager [José Mourinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mourinho "José Mourinho") because of his lack of pre-season training, which he missed as a result of his ongoing transfer negotiations.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37) The presence of veteran midfielders [Xabi Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xabi_Alonso "Xabi Alonso") and [Sami Khedira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Khedira "Sami Khedira") in defensive midfield, and Özil in offensive midfield, usually kept Modrić out of the starting line-up, limiting him to substitute appearances. He mostly played out-of-position for his first few months at the club. He played his first [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Champions_League "2012–13 UEFA Champions League") match for Real Madrid in the group stage against [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") on 18 September, which Madrid won 3–2. On 3 November, Modrić scored his first goal for Real Madrid in the last minute of their 4–0 victory over [Real Zaragoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Zaragoza "Real Zaragoza") in [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_La_Liga "2012–13 La Liga").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-96) His most notable match that year was on 4 December, when he assisted for the first two goals of [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") and [José Callejón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Callej%C3%B3n "José Callejón") with cross-field passes in a 4–1 victory over Ajax in the group stage of the Champions League.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-99) At the end of the year he was voted as the worst signing of the season by Spanish newspaper _[Marca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marca_\(newspaper\) "Marca \(newspaper\)")_.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-100)
Modrić started in Real Madrid's home match against rivals Barcelona on 2 March 2013. From a corner kick, he assisted [Sergio Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ramos "Sergio Ramos") to score the winning goal in the 82nd minute, giving Real a victory in _[El Clásico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Cl%C3%A1sico "El Clásico")_. On 5 March, Modrić came on as a second-half substitute during the decisive Champions League knockout leg against ten-man Manchester United at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford"). With Madrid behind by a goal, Modrić equalised with a long-range shot from 23 m (25 yd) out and played a key role in the rest of the match, which Real Madrid won 2–1, advancing them to the quarter-finals 3–2 on aggregate.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-103) This match is often seen as the turning point in Modrić's career in Real Madrid.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37) On 16 March, he replicated this performance against [Mallorca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Mallorca "RCD Mallorca"), giving Real Madrid the lead with a long-range volley from 27 m (30 yd); Real Madrid won the match 5–2.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-104) Modrić played as a starter in both Champions League semi-final matches against [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund"). In the first leg on 24 April, he played in the attacking midfield position where he did not influence the match and the team lost 4–1. On 30 April, in the second leg 2–0 victory, Modrić played as the deep-lying playmaker, making passes to the attackers and creating several chances; he was among the best-rated players that night.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-107) From March 2013, Modrić's form and influence in the midfield continued to improve, distinguishing himself as a player with most passes completed in his team. On 8 May, he assisted from the corner for the first goal and scored the fourth goal in a 6–2 victory over [Málaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1laga_CF "Málaga CF").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-108)
#### 2013–2015: Best midfielder in Spain and _La Décima_
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2013–2015: Best midfielder in Spain and La Décima") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section's source code: 2013–2015: Best midfielder in Spain and La Décima")]
> "He's the head of midfield in a complicated environment. Every day in Madrid pressure is coming at you from all sides. Modrić not only withstands the pressure but has grown among it to be Madrid's best player, with [[Cristiano] Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo")."
— [Predrag Mijatović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predrag_Mijatovi%C4%87 "Predrag Mijatović") praises Modrić's rising performance and significance for the team in January 2014.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-109)
With the arrival of new manager [Carlo Ancelotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Ancelotti "Carlo Ancelotti"), Modrić became one of the most frequent starters in the team, being partnered in midfield with Xabi Alonso to provide a balance of defence and attack.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-WhoScored2013-110)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-111) He was consistently the team's most efficient passer, averaging 90% accuracy in [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_La_Liga "2013–14 La Liga"), and also having the most ball recoveries among the squad.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Ice_Cold-55)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-WhoScored2013-110) He scored his first goal of the [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2013–14 Real Madrid CF season") in the last [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Champions League") group match against [Copenhagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F.C._Copenhagen "F.C. Copenhagen"), making it his fifth goal for the club, all five of which were scored from the outside the penalty area.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-112) Modrić scored his first goal of the Liga season in a 3–0 away win against [Getafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Getafe_CF "Getafe CF"), his sixth goal outside the penalty area.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-113) Modrić was on the pitch when Real Madrid won the [2013–14 Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Copa_del_Rey "2013–14 Copa del Rey") after defeating Barcelona 2–1 in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2014 Copa del Rey Final").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Maestro-114)
In the first leg of the Champions League quarter-finals, Modrić intercepted the ball and assisted Cristiano Ronaldo for the third goal in Real Madrid's 3–0 home victory against Borussia Dortmund. The goal was ultimately decisive because Real went on to lose 2–0 in the second leg, but progressed with a marginal aggregate score of 3–2. In his 100th appearance for the club,[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-115) Modrić assisted for the first goal in the second leg 4–0 victory over [Bayern Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich") in the Champions League semi-final, helping Real Madrid reach the final for the first time in 12 years.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-116) He was included in UEFA's Team of the Week for both legs of the semi-final.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-118) On 24 May in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2014 UEFA Champions League Final"), Modrić again assisted from a corner for teammate Sergio Ramos, who scored a 93rd-minute equaliser against [local rivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid_Derby "Madrid Derby") [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid"). Real won 4–1 in extra time, marking the club's tenth Champions League title, locally known as _La Décima_ (lit. 'the Tenth').[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-119) He was included in the UEFA Champions League Team of the Season[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CLTeam20134-120) and received the [LFP award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LFP_Awards "LFP Awards") for the "Best Midfielder" of the Spanish first division for that season.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-121)
In August 2014, Modrić signed a new contract to stay at Real Madrid until 2018.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-122) With the departure of Alonso he was partnered with newly arrived [Toni Kroos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Kroos "Toni Kroos").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Tweedale2014-123) Real Madrid began the [2014–15 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2014–15 Real Madrid CF season") by winning the [UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_UEFA_Super_Cup "2014 UEFA Super Cup") over [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC")[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-124) Modrić assisted twice for Bale, first against [Real Sociedad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Sociedad "Real Sociedad") in [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_La_Liga "2014–15 La Liga"),[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-125) and second against [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Basel "FC Basel") in the [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League "2014–15 UEFA Champions League").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-126)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-127) In the 2–0 away win against [Villarreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villarreal_CF "Villarreal CF"), Modrić scored his seventh goal from outside of the box.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-128)
In late November, Modrić sustained a thigh injury during an international match against [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"), because of which he did not play for three months.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-129) He returned in early March 2015, starting in seven matches and proving his form.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-130) On 21 April, in the 3–1 home win against Málaga, he strained ligaments in his right knee, because of which he did not play until May.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-131)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-133) With his injury, Real Madrid's 22-match winning run in the season came to an end. His absence and the lack of a quality substitute were seen as the main cause of Real Madrid's failure to win matches in La Liga and the Champions League.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-134) Ancelotti said, "Modrić has missed most of the year and this has hurt us."[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CollinsTim-135) Modrić's influence was recognised and he was selected by professional players in the [FIFA FIFPro World XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFPro#FIFA_FIFPRO_Men's_World_11 "FIFPro").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFPro-136)
#### 2015–2017: Among the world's best players and _La Undécima_ and _Duodécima_
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2015–2017: Among the world's best players and La Undécima and Duodécima") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section's source code: 2015–2017: Among the world's best players and La Undécima and Duodécima")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Shahter-Reak_M_2015_%2810%29.jpg/250px-Shahter-Reak_M_2015_%2810%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shahter-Reak_M_2015_\(10\).jpg)Modrić playing against [Shakhtar Donetsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Shakhtar_Donetsk "FC Shakhtar Donetsk") during their [group stage match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Group_A "2015–16 UEFA Champions League group stage") in the UEFA Champions League in November 2015
For the [2015–16 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2015–16 Real Madrid CF season"), Carlo Ancelotti was replaced by [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") under whom Modrić continued to be a key midfield player.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Master-137)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-138) He sustained a muscular groin injury during an international match against [Bulgaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria_national_football_team "Bulgaria national football team") in October, initially suggesting an absence of two-to-three weeks.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-139) However, by 20 October, he had recovered in time for the match against [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C.").[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-140)
With the arrival of new manager [Zinedine Zidane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zinedine_Zidane "Zinedine Zidane") in January 2016,[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-141) the relationship between them was noted in the media, with Modrić described as "master of the game",[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Master-137)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-142) and the crucial "connector" of the defence and attack.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Connector-143) It was seen in the first three matches, wins against [Deportivo La Coruña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_de_La_Coru%C3%B1a "Deportivo de La Coruña") and [Sporting Gijón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_de_Gij%C3%B3n "Sporting de Gijón") and a draw against [Real Betis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Betis "Real Betis"), in which Modrić was praised for creating chances, his positioning and overall performance and influence.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Master-137)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Connector-143)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-144) On 7 February, Modrić scored a winning goal from outside the box in a 1–2 away win against [Granada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granada_CF "Granada CF").[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-145) Modrić was a regular in the starting line-up when the team won the [2015–16 Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_UEFA_Champions_League "2015–16 UEFA Champions League") in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2016 UEFA Champions League Final") against Atlético.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-146) He was included in both Champions League,[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CL_2015/16_Team-147) and La Liga's team of the season.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-La_Liga_2015/16_Team-148) For the second time, he also received the [LFP award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LFP_Awards "LFP Awards") for the "Best Midfielder" of the Spanish first league.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-LFPAward2-149) He was for the second time included in the [FIFA FIFPro World XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFPro#FIFA_FIFPRO_Men's_World_11 "FIFPro").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFPro2-150)
On 18 October 2016, Modrić signed a new contract with Real Madrid, keeping him at the club until 2020.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-151) Due to injury of a left knee sustained in mid-September, he missed eight matches, returning early November.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-152) On 18 December, he won the [2016 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2016 FIFA Club World Cup") with Real Madrid, receiving the [Silver Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Club_World_Cup_awards#Golden_Ball "FIFA Club World Cup awards") for his performances during the tournament.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Awards-153) In January 2017, for the first time was included in the [UEFA Team of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Team_of_the_Year "UEFA Team of the Year") (2016).[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-UEFATOTY-154) On 12 March 2017, in a 2–1 win over Real Betis, Modrić played his 200th match for Real Madrid.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-155)
Modrić was a regular starter when Real Madrid won the [2016–17 La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_La_Liga "2016–17 La Liga"),[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-156)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-157) as well as the [2016–17 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_UEFA_Champions_League "2016–17 UEFA Champions League"), where he provided the assist for Cristiano Ronaldo's second goal in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2017 UEFA Champions League Final") against [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-158) Modrić was included in Champions League team of the season[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CL_2016/17_Team-159) and became the first Croatian to win the Champions League three times.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-160) He also received the [UEFA Club Football award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Club_Football_Awards "UEFA Club Football Awards") for Best Midfielder of the Champions League season.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CLMid2016-2017-161) In the competition for the [UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Men's_Player_of_the_Year_Award "UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award"), he came fourth,[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-162) while for [2017 Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Ballon_d'Or "2017 Ballon d'Or"), fifth.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-163) For the third time, he was also included in the [FIFA FIFPro World XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFPro#FIFA_FIFPRO_Men's_World_11 "FIFPro").[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFPro3-164)
#### 2017–18: Ballon d'Or and third consecutive Champions League title
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2017–18: Ballon d'Or and third consecutive Champions League title") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section's source code: 2017–18: Ballon d'Or and third consecutive Champions League title")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Liver-RM_%282%29.jpg/250px-Liver-RM_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Liver-RM_\(2\).jpg)Modrić (left) with [Gareth Bale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gareth_Bale "Gareth Bale") during the [2018 Champions League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2018 UEFA Champions League Final")
With the departure of [James Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Rodr%C3%ADguez "James Rodríguez") to Bayern Munich, Modrić inherited the team's coveted [number 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_number_\(association_football\) "Squad number \(association football\)") [jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kit_\(association_football\) "Kit \(association football\)") for the new [2017–18 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2017–18 Real Madrid CF season"), replacing his previous number 19 jersey.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-165) In December, he won the [2017 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2017 FIFA Club World Cup") with Real Madrid and received the [Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Club_World_Cup_awards#Golden_Ball "FIFA Club World Cup awards") award as the best player of the competition for his performance.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MarcaGolden-166) His first goal of the season came in a 7–1 win over Deportivo de La Coruña on 21 January 2018.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-167) In the same month was for the second time included in the [UEFA Team of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Team_of_the_Year "UEFA Team of the Year") (2017).[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-UEFATOTY17-168) Modrić was a regular starter when Real Madrid won the [2017–18 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League "2017–18 UEFA Champions League"), starting in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2018 UEFA Champions League Final") victory against Liverpool which saw Madrid win their third consecutive title.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-169) For his performances throughout the campaign, Modrić was included in Champions League team of the season for the third consecutive time.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CL_2017/18_Team-170) He later received the [UEFA Club Football Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Club_Football_Awards#Best_Midfielder "UEFA Club Football Awards") for Best Midfielder of the Champions League season for the second consecutive time.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CLMid2017-2018-171)
Due to his club, and national team performance at the [2018 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup"), where he also received the [Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_awards#Golden_Ball "FIFA World Cup awards"),[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFAGolden-172) in August and September Modrić won the [UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Men's_Player_of_the_Year_Award "UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award") and [The Best FIFA Men's Player Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Best_FIFA_Football_Awards_2018 "The Best FIFA Football Awards 2018"),[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-UEFAMPYA-173)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFAPYA-174) while in December, he added the [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Ballon_d'Or "2018 Ballon d'Or") to his personal tally,[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBCBallon-175) marking the first time since 2007 that the award was not won by [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") or Cristiano Ronaldo.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBCBallon-175)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-176)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-177) Furthermore, besides becoming the first Croatian player to win these awards,[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-178) Modrić was the first player to win both the World Cup Golden Ball and the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award in the same year since [Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldo_\(Brazilian_footballer\) "Ronaldo \(Brazilian footballer\)") in 1998,[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-179) and the World Cup Golden Ball and the Best FIFA Men's Player of the Year Award after [Romário](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rom%C3%A1rio "Romário") in 1994.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-180) Additionally, he is the first player to win the awards from the [former Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Former_Yugoslavia "Former Yugoslavia") territory, the first footballer from [Eastern Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Europe "Eastern Europe") to win a [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d'Or "Ballon d'Or") after [Andriy Shevchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andriy_Shevchenko "Andriy Shevchenko") in 2004,[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-181)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-182) and the tenth player from Real Madrid to capture the trophy.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-183) Furthermore, winning the trophy triggered a clause in his contract, ensuring his stay at the club until 2021.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-184) He was also included in the [FIFA FIFPro World XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFPro#FIFA_FIFPRO_Men's_World_11 "FIFPro") for the fourth time,[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFPro4-185) and won the [IFFHS World's Best Playmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_Football_History_&_Statistics#The_World's_Best_Playmaker "International Federation of Football History & Statistics") award.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-IFFHSPlay-186)
After receiving the FIFA Men's Player of the Year Award, Modrić stated it "shows that we all can become the best with hard work, dedication, and belief, all dreams can come true".[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-187) Modrić dedicated the Ballon d'Or to "all the players who probably deserved to win it and didn't" in the past decade, including [Xavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavi_\(footballer,_born_1980\) "Xavi \(footballer, born 1980\)"), [Andrés Iniesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Iniesta "Andrés Iniesta"), and [Wesley Sneijder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesley_Sneijder "Wesley Sneijder") among others.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBCBallon-175)
#### 2018–2021: Two-time champion of Spain
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2018–2021: Two-time champion of Spain") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section's source code: 2018–2021: Two-time champion of Spain")]
The arrival of new manager [Julen Lopetegui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julen_Lopetegui "Julen Lopetegui") in August 2018 saw Modrić given a steady return to the first team as a substitute due to his lack of pre-season training after the 2018 World Cup.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-188)[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-189) This included a substitute appearance in his team's 2–4 loss after extra time against Atlético Madrid in the [UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_UEFA_Super_Cup "2018 UEFA Super Cup").[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-190) His first start of the season came on 1 September in a 4–1 home win against [Leganés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD_Legan%C3%A9s "CD Leganés"), in which he assisted his side's third goal, scored by [Karim Benzema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karim_Benzema "Karim Benzema").[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-191) His 100th appearance in the UEFA club competition came on 19 September in a 3–0 home win against [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Roma "A.S. Roma"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-ElvirUEFA-22) in which he assisted the second goal, scored by Gareth Bale.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-192) On 22 December, Modrić won his third [FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2018 FIFA Club World Cup"), scoring the first goal and assisting for the third in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_Final "2018 FIFA Club World Cup Final") against [Al Ain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ain_FC "Al Ain FC").[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-193) On 13 and 19 January 2019, Modrić for the first time scored in two consecutive league games for Real Madrid, in a 1–2 away win against Real Betis and 2–0 home win against Sevilla.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-194)[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-195) In the same month was included in the [UEFA Team of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Team_of_the_Year "UEFA Team of the Year") (2018) for the third time in his career.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-UEFATOTY18-196) From 27 February to 5 March, Modrić went through what he described as "the most difficult week of his football life,"[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-197) with Real Madrid losing to Barcelona twice and Ajax and crashing out of [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Copa_del_Rey "2018–19 Copa del Rey"), [title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_La_Liga "2018–19 La Liga") race and the [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Champions_League "2018–19 UEFA Champions League"), respectively.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-198)[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-199)[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-200) Despite having had an underwhelming [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2018–19 Real Madrid CF season"),[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Siguero10919-201) for the fifth consecutive time he was included in the [FIFA FIFPro World XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFPro#FIFA_FIFPRO_Men's_World_11 "FIFPro").[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFPro5-202)
On 27 August 2019 was the seventh anniversary of Modrić's signing with the club.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-203) Although raising doubts due to age of 34 and decision to continue playing with the national team which makes him prone to injuries,[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-204) Modrić stated that wants to "recapture his best form this [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2019–20 Real Madrid CF season")".[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Siguero10919-201) His first goal of the season came on 5 October in a 4–2 home victory against Granada.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-205) On 12 November was awarded with a [Golden Foot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Foot "Golden Foot") award.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-MarcaGoldenFoot-206) On 23 November he made two assists and scored a goal in a 3–1 home victory against Real Sociedad.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-207) On 8 January 2020, Modrić with _[trivela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curl_\(association_football\) "Curl \(association football\)")_ scored his fifth goal of the season and 100th career goal in a 3–1 victory against [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") in the semi-finals of [2019–20 Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2019–20 Supercopa de España").[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-208) On 12 January he successfully converted a penalty in a [shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout "Penalty shootout") as Real Madrid beat Atlético 4–1 on penalties in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a_Final "2019–20 Supercopa de España Final").[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-209) Following the continuation of [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_La_Liga "2019–20 La Liga") after a three-month suspension due to [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Spain "COVID-19 pandemic in Spain"), Modrić was praised for being one of Real Madrid's best players despite his age, resulting in numerous media outlets wondering about prolongation of his contract with the club.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-210) On 16 July, he assisted Benzema's opening goal in a 2–1 victory over Villarreal, as Real Madrid secured the league title.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-211)[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-212)
On 21 October 2020, he scored his first goal of the [2020–21 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2020–21 Real Madrid CF season") in a [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_UEFA_Champions_League "2020–21 UEFA Champions League") 3–2 defeat to Shakhtar Donetsk.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-213) The goal made him the fourth player in the history of the club to score in the competition aged 35 or more, alongside [Alfredo Di Stéfano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfredo_Di_St%C3%A9fano "Alfredo Di Stéfano"), [Ferenc Puskás](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferenc_Pusk%C3%A1s "Ferenc Puskás") and [Francisco Gento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Gento "Francisco Gento").[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-214) It was named the Goal of the Week by UEFA.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-215) Three days later, he came off the bench to score with _trivela_ his first ever _Clásico_ goal, as Real Madrid defeated Barcelona 3–1.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-216)[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-217) On 25 May 2021, he extended his contract with Real Madrid until 2022.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-218)[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-219)
#### 2021–2024: Fourth La Liga, sixth Champions League, second Copa del Rey title
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=14 "Edit section: 2021–2024: Fourth La Liga, sixth Champions League, second Copa del Rey title") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section's source code: 2021–2024: Fourth La Liga, sixth Champions League, second Copa del Rey title")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Ofrenda_de_la_Liga_y_la_Champions-56-L.Mill%C3%A1n_%2852109788795%29.jpg/250px-Ofrenda_de_la_Liga_y_la_Champions-56-L.Mill%C3%A1n_%2852109788795%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ofrenda_de_la_Liga_y_la_Champions-56-L.Mill%C3%A1n_\(52109788795\).jpg)Modrić in a trophy presentation ceremony in front of [Almudena Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almudena_Cathedral "Almudena Cathedral") in May 2022
