On 24 October 2021 of [2021–22 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2021–22 Real Madrid CF season"), Modrić played his 400th game for Real Madrid in a 2–1 _Clásico_ victory.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-220) On 30 October, Modrić captained Real Madrid for the first time and assisted for the winning goal, after [Marcelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelo_\(footballer,_born_1988\) "Marcelo \(footballer, born 1988\)") had given him the armband upon being substituted off in the 2–1 victory over [Elche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elche_CF "Elche CF").[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-221)[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-222) On 7 December 2021, he played his 100th Champions League game and was named Man of the Match in a 2–0 victory over Inter Milan.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-223) On 16 January 2022, he scored the first goal in the [2022 Supercopa de España Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a_Final "2022 Supercopa de España Final") and was named Man of the Match, as Real Madrid defeated Athletic Bilbao 2–0.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-224) The goal made him the oldest goalscorer in the history of [the competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Supercopa de España").[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-225) On 5 March, Modrić assisted and scored from outside of the box in a 4–1 victory over Real Socidedad.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-226) On 6 and 12 April, Modrić assisted in both legs of Champions League [quarter-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_phase#Quarter-finals "2021–22 UEFA Champions League knockout phase") 5–4 aggregate victory against Chelsea. Praised for attacking and defensive performances in both games,[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-227)[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-228)[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-229) because of a long-range _trivela_ assist for [Rodrygo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodrygo "Rodrygo") in the crucial moment of the second leg was named Man of the Match as well as voted Player of the Week by UEFA.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-230)[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-231) His assist to Rodrygo has been called the "pass of the decade" by [Ally McCoist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ally_McCoist "Ally McCoist"),[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-232) and as "absolutely perfect, and it was just gorgeous to watch" by [Thierry Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Henry "Thierry Henry").[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-233) He was a regular starter on 30 April when Real Madrid won their 35th and his 3rd Spanish title,[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-234) on 4 May when Real Madrid won in extra time in the second leg against Manchester City, and on 28 May when he won his 5th title in the [final of Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2022 UEFA Champions League Final").[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-235)[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-236) For the sixth time in his career, he was included in the UEFA Champions League Squad of the Season.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CL_2021/22_Team-237) On 8 June 2022, he renewed his contract until 2023.[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-238)
On 20 August 2022, Modrić landed his first goal and assist of the [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2022–23 Real Madrid CF season") in a 4–1 away victory over [Celta Vigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RC_Celta_de_Vigo "RC Celta de Vigo") in a [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") fixture.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-239) On 6 September he scored in his first [Champions League game of the season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Champions_League_group_stage#Celtic_v_Real_Madrid "2022–23 UEFA Champions League group stage") in a 3–0 away victory against [Celtic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C."), becoming the eighth Real Madrid player with 100 appearances in the competition.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-240)[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-241) On 11 September, he became the third Real Madrid player after Puskás and [Francisco Buyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Buyo "Francisco Buyo") to play 100 games while over 35 years of age.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-242)[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-243) In February 2023, Modrić was included for the sixth time in the [FIFA FIFPro World XI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Best_FIFA_Football_Awards_2022#FIFA_FIFPRO_Men's_World_11 "The Best FIFA Football Awards 2022").[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFPro6-244) On 6 May, he played as a second-half substitute in a 2–1 win over [Osasuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna") in the [Copa del Rey final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Copa_del_Rey_final "2023 Copa del Rey final"), to achieve his second trophy in that tournament.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-245) In June, he extended his contract until 2024.[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-246)
During the [2023–24 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Real_Madrid_CF_season "2023–24 Real Madrid CF season"), with the departure of Benzema, Modrić became vice-captain of the team,[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-247) but also started to receive less playing time in the starting eleven due to change in formation and competition with younger players like [Federico Valverde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Valverde "Federico Valverde"), [Jude Bellingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jude_Bellingham "Jude Bellingham"), [Eduardo Camavinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Camavinga "Eduardo Camavinga"), [Aurélien Tchouaméni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aur%C3%A9lien_Tchouam%C3%A9ni "Aurélien Tchouaméni") and [Dani Ceballos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Ceballos "Dani Ceballos").[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-248)[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-249)[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-250) On 28 October, Modrić came on as a second-half substitute and made his 500th appearance for Real Madrid in all competitions in a 2–1 away win against Barcelona, to which he contributed with an assist to the last-minute winning goal by Bellingham.[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-251) On 27 November, in a 3–0 away win against [Cádiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A1diz_CF "Cádiz CF"), Modrić set the record for most club appearances after 35 years old, with 161 appearances, breaking the previous record he held with [Paco Buyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Buyo "Francisco Buyo").[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-252) On 30 April 2024, Modrić came on as a late substitute in the first match of the Champions League semi-final against Bayern Munich and, at the age of 38 years and 234 days, broke the record for the oldest Real Madrid player to make an appearance in the tournament, beating Puskás by five days.[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-253) A few days later, on 4 May, he became the oldest player to feature in La Liga for Real Madrid, at the age of 38 years and 238 days, breaking another record of Puskás, in a 3–0 win against Cádiz.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-254) Furthermore, he clinched his fourth [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_La_Liga "2023–24 La Liga") title with Real Madrid following that victory, thus matching Marcelo, Karim Benzema and [Nacho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacho_\(footballer,_born_1990\) "Nacho \(footballer, born 1990\)")'s record as the club's most decorated player with 25 trophies.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-255) He extended his record with his 26th trophy in the [Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2024 UEFA Champions League final"), following a 2–0 victory against Borussia Dortmund, same as for Nacho.[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-256) He also became the first player to win six finals in the competition, along with [Dani Carvajal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dani_Carvajal "Dani Carvajal").[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-257)
#### 2024–25: Captaincy, records, and departure
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2024–25: Captaincy, records, and departure") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section's source code: 2024–25: Captaincy, records, and departure")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Modric_in_LIV_VS_RMA_2024_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Modric_in_LIV_VS_RMA_2024_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Modric_in_LIV_VS_RMA_2024_\(cropped\).jpg)Modrić captaining Real Madrid in a [2024–25 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_UEFA_Champions_League "2024–25 UEFA Champions League") phase match against Liverpool in November 2024
On 17 July 2024, Modrić extended his contract until 2025 and became captain of the team following the departure of Nacho.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-258)[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-259) A month later, on 14 August, he achieved his fifth [Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_UEFA_Super_Cup "2024 UEFA Super Cup") trophy following a 2–0 victory over [Atalanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atalanta_BC "Atalanta BC"), becoming the lone most decorated player in the club's history with 27 titles.[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-260) On 19 October, he became the oldest player to feature in a competitive match for Real Madrid in a 2–1 away victory over Celta Vigo, aged 39 years and 40 days, surpassing previous record of Puskás in 1966.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-261)[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-262) Later that year, on 18 December, Modrić clinched his record-extending 28th title with the club following a 3–0 victory over [Pachuca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.F._Pachuca "C.F. Pachuca") in the [FIFA Intercontinental Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_FIFA_Intercontinental_Cup_final "2024 FIFA Intercontinental Cup final").[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-263)
On 3 January 2025, Modrić scored his first goal of the [2024–25 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_La_Liga "2024–25 La Liga") during a 2–1 away victory over Valencia, in which he became the oldest player to score for Real Madrid in all competitions, aged 39 years and 116 days, surpassing Ferenc Puskás's record set in 1966.[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-RMCF2025-264)[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-265) Additionally, he made his 561st appearance for the club, joining the top ten on Real Madrid's all-time appearances list, equalling the records of both [Pirri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirri "Pirri") and [Míchel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%ADchel_\(footballer,_born_1963\) "Míchel \(footballer, born 1963\)").[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-RMCF2025-264) On 23 February, Modrić was named Man of the Match and from a corner kick he scored a half-volley goal from 25 meters during a 2–0 away win over [Girona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girona_FC "Girona FC").[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-266)[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-267)[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-268)
Although Modrić played in almost 60 games and recorded more minutes, goals and assists than in the previous season, still showing top-tier quality and importance to the club's midfield,[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-269)[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-270) it was announced on 22 May 2025 that Modrić would leave Real Madrid after 13 years at the club, following the [2025 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2025 FIFA Club World Cup") in the United States.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-271)[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC220525-272) He played his last home game with the club at the Santiago Bernabéu on 24 May against Real Sociedad, receiving club's tribute, and both teams' players [guard of honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guard_of_honour#Association_football "Guard of honour") before the end of the game, due to his legacy.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-273)[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-274) [Guillem Balagué](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillem_Balagu%C3%A9 "Guillem Balagué") described it as the "end of an era" in the club's history.[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC220525-272) At the FIFA Club World Cup, Modrić played in all six of Real Madrid's matches as the club progressed to the [semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Semi-finals "2025 FIFA Club World Cup knockout stage"),[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-275)[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-276) where they were knocked out after losing 4–0 to Paris Saint-Germain.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-277)
### AC Milan
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=16 "Edit section: AC Milan") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section's source code: AC Milan")]
On 14 July 2025, Modrić joined [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") side [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") on a free transfer, signing a one-year contract with an optional one-year extension.[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-278)[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-279) His salary was set to $4 million with bonus add-ons.[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-280) He stated that playing for Milan was a childhood dream of his, growing up watching many Croatians play for the club.[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-281)[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-282) Upon Modrić's arrival his jersey became the club's top-selling, nearly off-setting his entire contract cost.[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-283)
He made his debut in the opening match of the season on 23 August against newly promoted [Cremonese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Cremonese "US Cremonese") at the [San Siro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Siro "San Siro") that ended in a 2–1 defeat,[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-284) but his performance was praised nonetheless.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-285)[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-286) On his debut, Modrić became the oldest player to make a debut in Serie A, surpassing the previous record held by [Empoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empoli_FC "Empoli FC") goalkeeper [Maurizio Pugliesi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurizio_Pugliesi "Maurizio Pugliesi").[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-287) In his second game, a 2–0 win away against [Lecce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Lecce "US Lecce"), Modrić made an assist and was Milan's MVP of the match.[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-288) In his third game, a home 1–0 win against [Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna_FC_1909 "Bologna FC 1909"), Modrić scored the winning and his first goal in Serie A, receiving Milan's MVP for the second time in a row.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-289)[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-290)
Over the course of the season, he quickly established himself as an important part of Milan's midfield, but in the final months he began to encounter physical difficulties.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-291) His campaign was ultimately cut short by a significant facial injury sustained in a Serie A match against [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") following a collision with [Manuel Locatelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_Locatelli "Manuel Locatelli"), which resulted in a fractured cheekbone and required surgery in April 2026.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-292)[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-293)
On 23 July 2026, Modrić signed a one-year extension with the club until 30 June 2027, confirming his second season for the _Rossoneri_.[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-294)[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-295)
## International career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=17 "Edit section: International career") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section's source code: International career")]
Modrić began his international career at youth level, playing for the Croatian [under-15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_under-15_football_team "Croatia national under-15 football team"), [under-17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_under-17_football_team "Croatia national under-17 football team"), [under-18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_under-18_football_team "Croatia national under-18 football team"), [under-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_under-19_football_team "Croatia national under-19 football team") and [under-21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_under-21_football_team "Croatia national under-21 football team") teams.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mid-38) He debuted in March 2001 for the under-15 team coached by [Martin Novoselac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Novoselac "Martin Novoselac"), but despite his talent and psychological maturity, he did not become a regular starter and leading player until his debuted for the under-18 team. Novoselac considers him a model for all young players due to his perseverance, sustained hard effort, and talent.[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAzpitartePuertas201644%E2%80%9345-296) Modrić made his full international debut for [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_football_team "Croatia national football team") on 1 March 2006 in a friendly match against [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national football team") in [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basel "Basel"), which Croatia won 3–2.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mid-38)
### 2006–2008: First major tournaments
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=18 "Edit section: 2006–2008: First major tournaments") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section's source code: 2006–2008: First major tournaments")]
Modrić made two appearances at the [2006 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup "2006 FIFA World Cup") finals as a substitute in the group fixtures against [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_national_football_team "Japan national football team")[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-297) and [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_men's_national_soccer_team "Australia men's national soccer team").[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-298) With the appointment of new manager Slaven Bilić, Modrić earned greater recognition at international level; he scored his first goal in Croatia's 2–0 friendly win over [world champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_FIFA_World_Cup_Final "2006 FIFA World Cup Final") Italy on 16 August 2006 in [Livorno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livorno "Livorno").[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-299)
Modrić's performances ensured a regular place in the international side and he gave a successful showing in Croatia's [UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008_qualifying_Group_E "UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying Group E"), which included home and away victories against [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team").[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-300)[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-301) As a young midfielder, much was expected of Modrić; he was often dubbed "the Croatian Cruyff".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Dutch-48)[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CruyffMarca-302) Modrić scored Croatia's first goal of [Euro 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008"), converting a penalty in the fourth minute of their 1–0 victory against hosts [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_national_football_team "Austria national football team") on 8 June 2008 and becoming the team's youngest ever goalscorer at the [European Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship") (aged 22 years and 273 days).[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-303)[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-:1-304) It was also the fastest penalty ever awarded and scored in the European Championships history.[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-305) He continued to impress at the tournament and was named [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") [Man of the Match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_of_the_Match "Man of the Match") in Croatia's next match when they defeated one of the pre-tournament favourites and eventual [finalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008_Final "UEFA Euro 2008 Final") [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_national_football_team "German national football team").[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-modricman-306) In the quarter-final against [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey_national_football_team "Turkey national football team"), Modrić took advantage of a mistake by veteran Turkish goalkeeper [Rüştü Reçber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%BC%C5%9Ft%C3%BC_Re%C3%A7ber "Rüştü Reçber"), and crossed to teammate [Ivan Klasnić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Klasni%C4%87 "Ivan Klasnić") for the first goal of the match with one minute of extra time remaining, but [Semih Şentürk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semih_%C5%9Eent%C3%BCrk "Semih Şentürk") almost immediately equalised for Turkey. In the ensuing penalty shootout, Modrić's kick was off-target and he failed to score the first penalty and Turkey won the shootout 3–1.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-307) At the end of the competition, Modrić was included in the [UEFA Team of the Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008#UEFA_Team_of_the_Tournament "UEFA Euro 2008"), becoming only the second Croatian to achieve this honour after [Davor Šuker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davor_%C5%A0uker "Davor Šuker").[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Dalje_2008-308)
### 2008–2016: Subsequent struggles
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=19 "Edit section: 2008–2016: Subsequent struggles") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section's source code: 2008–2016: Subsequent struggles")]
In the [2010 World Cup qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_Group_6 "2010 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 6"), Modrić scored three goals, against [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan_national_football_team "Kazakhstan national football team"),[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-309) [Andorra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andorra_national_football_team "Andorra national football team"),[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-310) and [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine_national_football_team "Ukraine national football team");[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-311) matching [Ivica Olić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivica_Oli%C4%87 "Ivica Olić"), [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić") and Eduardo. The team failed to qualify finishing one point behind second-placed Ukraine. After appearing in all of their [UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012_qualifying_Group_F "UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying Group F") matches and scoring a goal against [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_national_football_team "Israel national football team"),[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-312) Modrić started in all three of Croatia [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012_Group_C "UEFA Euro 2012 Group C") matches against the [Republic of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland_national_football_team "Republic of Ireland national football team"), Italy and [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team"), but the team failed to progress. His most notable performance was against Spain. The most memorable moment of the match came when Modrić picked the ball on the halfway line skipping Spain's midfield trio, rushing down on the right to reach the penalty area where he evaded a defender and with a _trivela_ crossed from 16 m (18 yd) to Ivan Rakitić, but [Iker Casillas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iker_Casillas "Iker Casillas") saved this attempt.[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-313)[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-314) Because Croatia did not advance from the group stage, Modrić was not included in the [Team of the Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012#Awards "UEFA Euro 2012"), although _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ included him in the best 11 until the semi-finals,[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-315) and his play was well received by critics.[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-316)[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-317)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Brazil_and_Croatia_match_at_the_FIFA_World_Cup_2014-06-12_%2810%29.jpg/250px-Brazil_and_Croatia_match_at_the_FIFA_World_Cup_2014-06-12_%2810%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brazil_and_Croatia_match_at_the_FIFA_World_Cup_2014-06-12_\(10\).jpg)Modrić playing against [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team") at the [2014 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup")
After the [playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_second_round "2014 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA second round"), Modrić with the Croatian team qualified for the [2014 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"). They entered [Group A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_A "2014 FIFA World Cup Group A") with hosts [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team"), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_national_football_team "Mexico national football team") and [Cameroon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameroon_national_football_team "Cameroon national football team"). Croatia played the opening match against Brazil, which they lost 3–1,[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-318) and Modrić sustained a minor foot injury.[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-319)[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-320) In the second match, Croatia won 4–0 against Cameroon,[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-321) but did not progress to the knockout stage after losing 3–1 to Mexico,[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-322) despite the great expectations from the Croatian press and public.[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-323)
In the [Euro 2016 qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016_qualifying_Group_H "UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying Group H") rounds, Modrić scored his first goals for Croatia in three years, the first against [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta_national_football_team "Malta national football team") on his 29th birthday with a long-range shot,[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-324) then a penalty against [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan_national_football_team "Azerbaijan national football team").[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-325) On 3 March 2015, Modrić captained Croatia for the first time, in an away draw against Azerbaijan.[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-326) In the [tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016") proper, Modrić scored the match-winning goal in Croatia's opening [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016_Group_D "UEFA Euro 2016 Group D") match against Turkey, a [volley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volley_\(football\) "Volley \(football\)") from 25 metres (28 yards).[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Match_vs_Turkey-327) In so doing, he became the first Croatian to score at the finals of two separate European Championships, having previously scored against Austria in 2008.[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-328) He was named Man of the Match.[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Match_vs_Turkey-327) Modrić was forced to miss the crucial fixture against Spain on 21 June because of a minor muscle injury.[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-329)[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-330) However, Croatia won and topped the group,[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-331) but lost to [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team") 0–1 in extra-time in the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016_knockout_phase#Croatia_vs_Portugal "UEFA Euro 2016 knockout phase").[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-332)
### 2016–2018: Golden Ball of the 2018 World Cup
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=20 "Edit section: 2016–2018: Golden Ball of the 2018 World Cup") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section's source code: 2016–2018: Golden Ball of the 2018 World Cup")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/ISL-HRV_%287%29.jpg/250px-ISL-HRV_%287%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ISL-HRV_\(7\).jpg)Modrić captaining Croatia at the [2018 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup")
For Croatia's [2018 World Cup qualifying campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_Group_I "2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group I"), Modrić became the new team captain, following [Darijo Srna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darijo_Srna "Darijo Srna")'s retirement.[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-333) Croatia started the campaign well; however, following 1–0 defeats to [Iceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceland_national_football_team "Iceland national football team")[[334]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-334) and Turkey[[335]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-335) and a 1–1 draw with [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland_national_football_team "Finland national football team") (in which Modrić made his [100th appearance for the national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_men's_footballers_with_100_or_more_international_caps "List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps")),[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-336)[[337]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-337) Croatia seriously compromised their qualification for the tournament.[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-338)[[339]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-339) This caused Modrić to publicly state his lack of confidence in coach [Ante Čačić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ante_%C4%8Ca%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Ante Čačić").[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-340)[[341]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-341)[[342]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-342) Čačić was soon replaced by [Zlatko Dalić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatko_Dali%C4%87 "Zlatko Dalić") ahead of Croatia's final qualifier against Ukraine away,[[343]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-343) which Croatia won 2–0 and won a place in the [play-offs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_second_round "2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA second round").[[344]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-344) Modrić scored a penalty in the 4–1 victory over [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece_national_football_team "Greece national football team") in the second qualifying round,[[345]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-345) enabling his team to qualify for the World Cup.
Croatia were placed in [Group D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_D "2018 FIFA World Cup Group D") alongside Argentina, Iceland and [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria_national_football_team "Nigeria national football team"). During the tournament, Modrić—along with Ivan Rakitić and Mario Mandžukić—were referred to as [Croatia's second "Golden Generation"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_national_football_team#Dali%C4%87's_second_"golden_generation"_\(2017%E2%80%932019\) "Croatia national football team").[[346]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-346)[[347]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-347) In Croatia's opening win against Nigeria, Modrić once again successfully executed a penalty kick and was named Man of the Match.[[348]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-348)[[349]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-349) He also scored in Croatia's subsequent 3–0 win over Argentina with a long-range shot from 23 m (25 yd),[[350]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-350) also being named Man of the Match.[[351]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-351)[[352]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-352) After also featuring in the final group stage match, against Iceland, his performances in the first round of the tournament saw him ranked by _[FourFourTwo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FourFourTwo "FourFourTwo")_ , _The Daily Telegraph_ and [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") as the best player of the group stage.[[353]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-353)[[354]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-354)[[355]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-355)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Modri%C4%87_World_Cup_2018.jpg/250px-Modri%C4%87_World_Cup_2018.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Modri%C4%87_World_Cup_2018.jpg)Modrić during the 2018 World Cup
In the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Croatia_vs_Denmark "2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") against [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark_national_football_team "Denmark national football team") on 1 July, with the score tied at 1–1, Modrić created a goalscoring opportunity for [Ante Rebić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ante_Rebi%C4%87 "Ante Rebić") in the second half of extra-time, who was brought down in the penalty area; Modrić proceeded to take the penalty, but his strike was saved by [Kasper Schmeichel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasper_Schmeichel "Kasper Schmeichel"). However, Modrić managed to score his spot-kick during the ensuing penalty shoot-out and Croatia advanced to the next round following a 3–2 victory on penalties.[[356]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-356)[[357]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-357)[[358]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-358) In the [quarter-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Russia_vs_Croatia "2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") against hosts [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia_national_football_team "Russia national football team") on 7 July, Modrić provided an assist in extra-time for [Domagoj Vida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domagoj_Vida "Domagoj Vida") from a corner kick, and once again scored in the victorious penalty shoot-out following a 2–2 draw; he was named Man of the Match for the third time in the tournament.[[359]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-359)[[360]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-360) In the semi-final against England on 11 July, Croatia advanced to the [World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup_Final "2018 FIFA World Cup Final") for the first time in their history following a 2–1 victory in extra time.[[361]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-361) It was reported two days before the final match that Modrić ran the most miles out of any player and was third by created chances, as well had most dribbles per match and completed passes in the opponent's half in his team.[[362]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-362) Although Croatia were beaten 4–2 by [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_national_football_team "France national football team") in the final on 15 July,[[363]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-McNulty-363) Modrić was awarded the [Golden Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_awards#Golden_Ball "FIFA World Cup awards") for the best player of the tournament,[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFAGolden-172) and was included in the [Team of the Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup#Dream_Team "2018 FIFA World Cup").[[364]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFATEAM1-364)[[365]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FIFATEAM2-365) After the squad's huge welcome in Zagreb,[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-366) Modrić and his teammates [Danijel Subašić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danijel_Suba%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Danijel Subašić"), [Šime Vrsaljko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%A0ime_Vrsaljko "Šime Vrsaljko") and [Dominik Livaković](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominik_Livakovi%C4%87 "Dominik Livaković") were welcomed by tens of thousands of people in their hometown of Zadar.[[367]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-367)
Modrić took part in all four matches in the [inaugural edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Nations_League "2018–19 UEFA Nations League") of the [UEFA Nations League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Nations_League "UEFA Nations League") as Croatia finished at the bottom of [Group A4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Nations_League_A#Group_4 "2018–19 UEFA Nations League A") following historical 6–0 away defeat to Spain in September and a 2–1 defeat to England at the [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium") in November 2018.[[368]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-368)[[369]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-369)
### 2019–2022: Bronze Ball of the 2022 World Cup
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=21 "Edit section: 2019–2022: Bronze Ball of the 2022 World Cup") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section's source code: 2019–2022: Bronze Ball of the 2022 World Cup")]
During the [Euro 2020 qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020_qualifying_Group_E "UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying Group E") rounds, Modrić scored two goals; a penalty in the away 1–1 draw with Azerbaijan and a solo-effort in the home 3–0 victory over [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_national_football_team "Hungary national football team") as Croatia topped the group and qualified for the [tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020 "UEFA Euro 2020").[[370]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-370)[[371]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-371) However, due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Europe "COVID-19 pandemic in Europe"), the tournament was postponed for a year.[[372]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-372) On 24 March 2021, Modrić made his 134th appearance for the national team in a 1–0 [2022 World Cup qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_%E2%80%93_UEFA_Group_H "2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group H") defeat to [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia_national_football_team "Slovenia national football team"), equalling Darijo Srna as the most capped player in the history of the team.[[373]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-373) Three days later, in a 1–0 World Cup qualifying victory over [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus_national_football_team "Cyprus national football team"), he surpassed Srna's record.[[374]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-374)[[375]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-375)
Modrić was selected to the [final squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020_squads#Croatia "UEFA Euro 2020 squads") for the UEFA Euro 2020 on 17 May.[[376]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-376) Despite Croatia's poor showings in their first two [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020_Group_D "UEFA Euro 2020 Group D") games, Modrić was named the Man of the Match in the second one, a 1–1 draw with the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic_national_football_team "Czech Republic national football team") on 18 June.[[377]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-377) Four days later, in the 3–1 victory over [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland_national_football_team "Scotland national football team"), with a _[trivela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curl_\(association_football\) "Curl \(association football\)")_ he scored Croatia's second goal and provided [Ivan Perišić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Peri%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Ivan Perišić") with an assist for the third goal as Croatia progressed to the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020_knockout_phase#Round_of_16 "UEFA Euro 2020 knockout phase").[[378]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-378) Modrić's goal made him Croatia's oldest ever goalscorer at the European Championships (aged 35 years and 286 days), while simultaneously holding the record for the youngest goalscorer that he set in 2008.[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-:1-304)
During the 2022 World Cup qualifying, Modrić scored three times and assisted twice in seven appearances.[[379]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-379) On 13 June 2022, he scored a penalty in a 1–0 away win over France in the [2022–23 UEFA Nations League A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Nations_League_A#Group_1 "2022–23 UEFA Nations League A"), to be Croatia's first ever win against the latter.[[380]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-380) On 25 September, he scored opening goal in the last group's game and 3–1 away victory against Austria,[[381]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-381) helping the team advance to the [2023 UEFA Nations League Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Nations_League_Finals "2023 UEFA Nations League Finals").[[382]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-382) On 9 November, Modrić was selected to Croatia's [final squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_squads#Croatia "2022 FIFA World Cup squads") for the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup").[[383]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-383) In the first and third [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_Group_F "2022 FIFA World Cup Group F") games against [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco_national_football_team "Morocco national football team") and [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium_national_football_team "Belgium national football team"), he was named the Man of the Match.[[384]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-384) He became the first player to play in both the European Championship and the World Cup in three different decades.[[385]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-385) In the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Japan_vs_Croatia "2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") and [quarter-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Croatia_vs_Brazil "2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"), Croatia advanced on penalties against Japan and Brazil, with Modrić scoring in the shoot-out against Brazil,[[386]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-386)[[387]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-387) and captaining Croatia to a second consecutive World Cup [semi-final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Argentina_vs_Croatia "2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage") where they lost 3–0 to Argentina. In the [third place play-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_knockout_stage#Third_place_play-off "2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage"),[[388]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-388) Croatia prevailed 2–1 over Morocco to secure a bronze medal.[[389]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-third-389)[[390]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-390) Modrić won the [Bronze Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Bronze_Ball "FIFA World Cup Bronze Ball").[[391]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-FifaBronzeBall-391)
Produced by [Fulwell 73](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulwell_73 "Fulwell 73"), [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA") released _Captains_ in 2022, an eight-part sports [docuseries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Docuseries "Docuseries") following six national team captains including Modrić in their respective [2022 FIFA World Cup qualification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification "2022 FIFA World Cup qualification") campaigns.[[392]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-:02-392)[[393]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-393)
### 2023–2025: Nations League finals and Euro 2024 disappointment
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=22 "Edit section: 2023–2025: Nations League finals and Euro 2024 disappointment") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section's source code: 2023–2025: Nations League finals and Euro 2024 disappointment")]
On 25 March 2023, in a [UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024_qualifying_Group_D "UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying Group D") match against [Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wales_national_football_team "Wales national football team"), Modrić became the oldest ever player to play a game for Croatia―aged 37 years, 6 months and 16 days―surpassing [Dražen Ladić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dra%C5%BEen_Ladi%C4%87 "Dražen Ladić")'s record set in 1999.[[394]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-394)
On 14 June 2023, Modrić was widely praised for his performance as he led Croatia to victory over Netherlands (4–2, a.e.t.) at the [De Kuip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip") in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), in the semi-finals of the [2023 UEFA Nations League Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Nations_League_Finals "2023 UEFA Nations League Finals").[[395]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-395) In the match, Modrić won a [penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_\(association_football\) "Penalty kick \(association football\)") being brought down by [Cody Gakpo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Gakpo "Cody Gakpo"), which was converted by [Andrej Kramarić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrej_Kramari%C4%87 "Andrej Kramarić"). As the game went to [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_\(sports\) "Overtime \(sports\)"), he assisted [Bruno Petković](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Petkovi%C4%87 "Bruno Petković") for the winner and closed the win scoring a penalty himself. Modrić was subsequently named Man of the match.[[396]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-396)[[397]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-397)[[398]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-398)[[399]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-399) Modrić finished second place as Croatia eventually lost to Spain 5–4 on penalties in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Nations_League_final "2023 UEFA Nations League final"), one of which he scored, following a 0–0 draw after extra time.[[400]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-400)
On 20 May 2024, Modrić was included in the [final squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024_squads#Croatia "UEFA Euro 2024 squads") for the [UEFA Euro 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024 "UEFA Euro 2024").[[401]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-401) He became one of only three players to feature in five European Championships.[[402]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-402) In the last [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2024_Group_B#Croatia_vs_Italy "UEFA Euro 2024 Group B") match against [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"), he had his penalty saved by [Gianluigi Donnarumma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluigi_Donnarumma "Gianluigi Donnarumma"), but scored a goal a minute later, becoming the oldest goalscorer at the European competition and overpassing [Ivica Vastić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivica_Vasti%C4%87 "Ivica Vastić") for 32 days.[[403]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-403) He was awarded player of the match, despite a stoppage-time equaliser from [Mattia Zaccagni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattia_Zaccagni "Mattia Zaccagni") that resulted in a 1–1 draw, which eliminated his team from the tournament.[[404]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-404) In March 2025, at the [2024–25 UEFA Nations League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_UEFA_Nations_League "2024–25 UEFA Nations League") quarter-finals, he captained Croatia against France, ultimately losing on penalties.[[405]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-405)[[406]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-406)
### 2026: Fifth World Cup
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=23 "Edit section: 2026: Fifth World Cup") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section's source code: 2026: Fifth World Cup")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Luka_Modric_Croatia_v_Portugal_2_July_2026-121.jpg/250px-Luka_Modric_Croatia_v_Portugal_2_July_2026-121.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Luka_Modric_Croatia_v_Portugal_2_July_2026-121.jpg)Modrić versus [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team") in the 2026 FIFA World Cup
On 18 May 2026, he was selected in the 26-man squad for the [2026 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_FIFA_World_Cup "2026 FIFA World Cup"), marking his fifth World Cup appearance.[[407]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-407) On 17 June, Modrić featured in Croatia's opening 4–2 defeat versus [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team"), becoming the second European player to make an appearance at 10 different major tournaments.[[408]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-408) On 23 June, he made his 200th international appearance for Croatia in a 1–0 victory over [Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_national_football_team "Panama national football team"), becoming the fourth player in history to reach this milestone.[[409]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-409)[[410]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-410) On 27 June, he provided an assist in a 2–1 victory over [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana_national_football_team "Ghana national football team") as his nation progressed to the knockout phase, becoming the oldest player to provide an assist at a World Cup at 40 years and 291 days.[[411]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-411) Modrić's side was knocked out by [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team") after a 2–1 defeat in [BMO Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMO_Field "BMO Field"), [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), where an equalising 103rd-minute stoppage-time goal from [Joško Gvardiol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo%C5%A1ko_Gvardiol "Joško Gvardiol") was controversially disallowed as offside by [VAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_assistant_referee "Video assistant referee").[[412]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-412)
## Player profile
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Player profile") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section's source code: Player profile")]
### Style of play
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Style of play") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section's source code: Style of play")]
> "Not only is he a very hard worker, he has a good brain and he provided some calmness and composure to the [midfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfield "Midfield"). His passing was neat and his contribution was outstanding. He was not only winning the ball, he was passing well. We thought that he was very influential. He did not just work hard, he made the other people play well around him".
— [Gérard Houllier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%A9rard_Houllier "Gérard Houllier"), UEFA Technical Team, 2008[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-modricman-306)
A diminutive and technically gifted midfielder, Modrić is typically deployed as a creative [playmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playmaker "Playmaker") and sets the tempo of the match by controlling possession from the middle of the pitch. He has been widely applauded by many footballing pundits, managers, and fellow players for his swift passing and long range shots, both often in the style of the _[trivela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curl_\(association_football\) "Curl \(association football\)")_ technique, as well as his composure and ability to evade tackles under pressure.[[413]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-ESPN-413)[[414]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-414)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Ice_Cold-55)[[415]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-415)[[416]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-416)[[417]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-417) He is noted for his tactical intelligence and versatility in both attack and defence, as well as his vision, interpretation of space, and [work rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Work_rate "Work rate").[[418]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-418) A former [attacking midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attacking_midfielder "Attacking midfielder"), Modrić is considered a veteran of the "pre-[assist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assist_\(association_football\) "Assist \(association football\)")" or build-up play, often creating space and time for his teammates to shoot or deliver goal-bound passes to other players.[[419]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-TheHail2017-419)[[420]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Matchett-420)[[421]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-421)[[422]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-star_dell'Europeo-422) He is also effective at taking [set pieces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_piece_\(football\) "Set piece \(football\)"), particularly [corners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corner_kick "Corner kick") or wide [free kicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_kick_\(association_football\) "Free kick \(association football\)").[[423]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-423)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Luka_Modric_2015.jpg/250px-Luka_Modric_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Luka_Modric_2015.jpg)Modrić was regarded as an emblematic "box-to-box" playmaker with [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF").
Modrić has been integral to the success of both Real Madrid and the Croatia national team, having won numerous individual honours for his contributions to club and country.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-CollinsTim-135)[[424]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-424) His play-style has earned him several nicknames as dubbed by the media and fandom, including "the midfield maestro", "the magician", "the puppet master", among a variety of others.[[425]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-425)[[419]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-TheHail2017-419)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Maestro-114)[[426]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-426)[[427]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-427)[[428]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-428)
### Position
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Position") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section's source code: Position")]
Modrić's complex game has brought him consistent success in the clubs for which he has played. Initially a [trequartista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trequartista "Trequartista") or attacking midfielder at Dinamo Zagreb and in his early career at Tottenham, in the 2010–11 season he flourished in a central midfield role as a [deep-lying playmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep-lying_playmaker "Deep-lying playmaker") (regista) who conducts the attack and creates chances for teammates.[[429]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-WhoscoredAsset11-429) Afterwards, Modrić acknowledged the role that [Harry Redknapp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Redknapp "Harry Redknapp") played in shaping of his deep-lying style, saying that dropping back enabled him "to read the game better" and show his full "creativity".[[430]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-430) Although a [central midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_midfielder "Central midfielder"), Modrić is also a hard-working player who has been seen to adopt a [defensive midfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_midfield "Defensive midfield") role in addition to playmaking, tracking back to win the ball from the opposition and prepare for a counter-attack, making him one of the most versatile players in the world, capable of playing in several [midfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder "Midfielder") positions.[[431]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-modricability-431)[[432]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-432) According to [Jonathan Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Wilson_\(writer\) "Jonathan Wilson \(writer\)"), in a 4–2–3–1 system Modrić is a third type of a [holding midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holding_midfielder "Holding midfielder"), being "neither entirely destructive or creative", but a "carrier" who – courtesy of his dribbling ability and attacking drive – is "capable of making late runs or carrying the ball at his feet", but in his case "with a hint of _regista_ ".[[433]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-433)[[434]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-434)[[435]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-435) As such, his role has also been likened to that of a _[mezzala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mezzala "Mezzala")_ , in Italian football jargon, namely an offensive–minded [box-to-box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box-to-box "Box-to-box") or central midfielder.[[422]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-star_dell'Europeo-422)
The switch to a more deep-lying position reduced his number of assists and goals, as well as his shot per game count (1.2), although his game was no longer based on being a goal threat; despite this, he had the second-highest count of key passes per game (2.06) in the team, as well as a very high pass accuracy rate (87%), with the highest passes per game count (62.5) in the team, the most long balls per game (5.6), the most successful [dribbles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dribbling#Association_football "Dribbling") (2.2), interceptions (2.5), and the highest tackle (1.9) count per game among others, high statistics which placed him amongst the top midfielders of the Premier League.[[429]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-WhoscoredAsset11-429)[[436]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-436) By the 2011–12 season statistically he was among the top-rated central and all-round midfielders across the [top five leagues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Five_\(association_football\) "Big Five \(association football\)"), alongside players like [Xabi Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xabi_Alonso "Xabi Alonso"), [Andrea Pirlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Pirlo "Andrea Pirlo"), [Bastian Schweinsteiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bastian_Schweinsteiger "Bastian Schweinsteiger") and [Xavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavi_\(footballer,_born_1980\) "Xavi \(footballer, born 1980\)").[[437]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-437)[[438]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-438)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Real_Madrid_v_Sevilla_February_10%2C_2013_B_13.JPG/250px-Real_Madrid_v_Sevilla_February_10%2C_2013_B_13.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Real_Madrid_v_Sevilla_February_10,_2013_B_13.JPG)Modrić converting a build-up play against [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") in 2013
Upon Modrić's arrival to Real Madrid, his midfield position was described as [numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squad_number_\(association_football\) "Squad number \(association football\)") six (defensive), eight (central) or ten (attacking), depending on the tactics,[[439]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Mourinho_on_LM-439) and his role was described as the second deep-lying pivot alongside Xabi Alonso in the 2012–13 season, a classic deep-lying playmaker whose creativity was needed to dictate his team's play and unlock the opposing defence.[[440]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-SN_Plan_C-440)[[441]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-441) In the first half of the 2013–14 season, during which he formed an effective central midfield partnership with Alonso and [Ángel Di María](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81ngel_Di_Mar%C3%ADa "Ángel Di María"), Modrić made more tackles (56) than any other Real Madrid player in La Liga with an average number of 2.86 tackles per match, as well as making the most completed passes (878) in the opposition half of the pitch among Real Madrid players, with the highest passing accuracy in La Liga (90%, also the highest of any midfielder in Europe's top five leagues who have made five or more assists during the season).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37) He produced the highest count of passes (60.7–64.7) and key passes per match (0.8–1.2) within the team.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Tweedale2014-123)[[442]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-442) Modrić's average passing accuracy during the season was between 91.6% and 92%, while his highest completion rate in a single match occurred in October 2014 against Barcelona when he completed all 42 attempted passes.[[443]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-443) That year Modrić's dribble attempts (75) at a success rate of 76% were second in Europe's top five leagues.[[444]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-444) During the 2015–16 season, although he placed only 12th in terms of chances created, almost all players above him were either forwards or attacking midfielders with no defensive responsibilities.[[420]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Matchett-420) Similar statistics followed his arrival to [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") in 2025, where the 40-year-old Modrić led Europe's Big Five leagues in pass completions (98.8%).[[445]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-445)

## Business ventures
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Business ventures") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section's source code: Business ventures")]
Aside from playing football, Modrić has embarked on a variety of business ventures. In 2020, he founded real estate company Modrić Family SL in Madrid.[[474]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-HRTInv2025-474) In 2022, he invested in Croatian-American startup company Sportening and three years later became a 50% co-owner of Zeppelin Craft Brewery in Croatia.[[475]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-475)[[474]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-HRTInv2025-474) In April 2025, Modrić became a minority co-owner of Welsh football club [Swansea City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swansea_City_A.F.C. "Swansea City A.F.C.").[[476]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-476)[[477]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-477) During the 2010s and 2020s, Modrić featured in endorsement campaigns for [Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike,_Inc. "Nike, Inc."), [Hublot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hublot "Hublot"), [Ožujsko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O%C5%BEujsko "Ožujsko"), and [Panini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panini_Group "Panini Group"), among others.[[478]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-478) Throughout 2026, he was a global brand ambassador for [Kalshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalshi "Kalshi"), an American prediction markets company.[[479]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-479)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Personal life") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section's source code: Personal life")]
Modrić married Vanja Bosnić in May 2010 in the Croatian capital [Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagreb "Zagreb") in a private ceremony after four years of dating,[[480]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-480) and a year later in the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church").[[481]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-481) They have three children.[[482]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Football_star_Luka_Modric_becomes_a_father-482)[[483]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-Modric_family_idyll-483)[[484]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-484)[[485]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-485) Modrić is a cousin of Australian footballer [Mark Viduka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Viduka "Mark Viduka"),[[486]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-486) and the godfather of [Mateo Kovačić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mateo_Kova%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Mateo Kovačić")'s son Ivan.[[487]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-487) Modrić generally maintains a low profile outside of football.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-BBC_Interview2014-37)[[488]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-488)
In late 2019, Modrić released his [autobiography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autobiography "Autobiography") _Moja igra_ (_My Game_), co-written by prominent Croatian sports journalist Robert Matteoni.[[489]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-489)[[490]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-490)

### Legal issues
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&veaction=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Legal issues") | [edit source](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luka_Modri%C4%87&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section's source code: Legal issues")]
Modrić was called to testify in an [embezzlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embezzlement "Embezzlement") and [tax evasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_evasion "Tax evasion") trial in 2018 against the former Dinamo Zagreb executive, [Zdravko Mamić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zdravko_Mami%C4%87 "Zdravko Mamić").[[493]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-:0-493) Modrić [annexed](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/annex "wiktionary:annex") most of his Tottenham transfer fee to Mamić because he brokered the transfer.[[494]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-494)[[495]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-495) Modrić was [charged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criminal_charge "Criminal charge") with [perjury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury") for stating that he annexed his fee at an earlier date than he allegedly had.[[493]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-:0-493) "My conscience is clear", he told the judge with the backing of the [Croatian Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_Football_Federation "Croatian Football Federation").[[496]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-SkyBate-496) The trial drew a mixed response from the Croatian public; some saw it as emblematic of corruption in Croatian football while others supported Modrić as he dealt with the situation during the [2018 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup "2018 FIFA World Cup").[[497]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-497)[[498]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-498) Later that year, the Croatian courts dismissed the perjury charge.[[499]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-499)[[500]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modri%C4%87#cite_note-500)

A small stone house by the side of the road, the last one before the rocky slopes of the Velebit mountains. Six and a half kilometres from my parents' home in Zaton Obrovački. This house was the centre of my little world until 1991, when we had to run away. This is where my father's parents lived: Grandpa Luka and Grandma Jela. My grandfather was a road mender, who maintained the old state road that connected Dalmatia and Lika, the coast and the mountains of Croatia. My grandmother was a housekeeper, a hardworking and modest woman. The house they lived in was owned by the road maintenance company, but back then I knew it only as my grandparents' home. We called it the 'upper house'. I never met my other grandfather, Petar, my mothers's father. He died before I was born. His wife, Grandma Manda, still lives in Obrovac. My parents worked at Trio Clothes Factory in Obrovac, four kilometres from our house. That's where they met.
